newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Royalties not holding up Argyle diamonds - minister.
newsitem.headline: Royalties not holding up Argyle diamonds - minister.

text.p: A four-year-old royalty disagreement was not holding up a planned $A200 million underground mine at the Argyle diamond project, Western Australian Resources Minister Colin Barnett said on Friday.

"Discussions about royalties on underground mining haven't even been progressed," Barnett said in response to an article in Business Review Weekly magazine. Barnett said the royalty issue was not part of the decision on whether to build the mine.
"The big issue will be whether Argyle want to spend $A200 million on underground mining. That is far more important that the royalty issue," he told a news conference.
The Argyle mine is 59.9 percent owned by Rio Tinto Plc/Ltd and 40.1 percent by Ashton Mining Ltd.

The magazine article said Australia's diamond industry was in crisis over the disagreement. It said the state government had drafted but not issued a default notice alleging the Argyle partners owe more than A$12 million in unpaid royalties.

Barnett confirmed there was a "commercial difference" of opinion over the calculation of the royalty in relation to a diamond stockpile built up by Argyle since 1994 but said the amount in dispute was only "several millions of dollars".
"It is my intention to serve default and I've indicated to Argyle perhaps two weeks ago that I would proceed with that," Barnett said.

"There is one last attempt to try and reach an agreed resolution ... but I think at this stage that if it is not resolved in the next week or so the government will formally issue default which will trigger a commercial arbitration," the minister said.
